newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Shekel weakens after Bank of Israel intervenes.
newsitem.headline: Shekel weakens after Bank of Israel intervenes.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened slightly on Monday against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies after the Bank of Israel intervened several times in the market to buy dollars, dealers said.
"The shekel was stable during the day but the Bank of Israel had to intervene several times in trading to keep the basket at seven percent below the slope," said Gideon Sadeh at Bank Leumi.

The shekel is allowed to trade in a band of seven percent above or below a sloping midpoint designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against a basket of currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.
"Activity was mixed today with slightly more conversions of shekels into foreign currency. The representative rate for the basket was set at seven percent below the slope," Sadeh said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.1920 against 3.1910 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5644 shekels against 3.5638 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8593 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8659 on Friday and against the mark at 2.0855 shekels per mark against 2.0861 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1920 shekels.
